hook.en: Newton realised that the force pulling an apple down is the same force that keeps the Moon in its orbit. One law for the falling fruit and for the whole sky.
hook.kn: ಸೇಬನ್ನು ಕೆಳಕ್ಕೆ ಎಳೆಯುವ ಬಲವೇ ಚಂದ್ರನನ್ನು ಕಕ್ಷೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹಿಡಿದಿಟ್ಟಿದೆ ಎಂದು ನ್ಯೂಟನ್ ಅರಿತುಕೊಂಡ. ಬೀಳುವ ಹಣ್ಣಿಗೂ ಇಡೀ ಆಕಾಶಕ್ಕೂ ಒಂದೇ ನಿಯಮ.

body.en: Every body in the universe attracts every other body with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them: $F = Gm_1m_2/r^2$. The force acts along the line joining them, and the forces on the two bodies are equal and opposite. For points outside a uniform sphere, the sphere attracts as if all its mass were at its centre.
body.kn: ವಿಶ್ವದ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಕಾಯವೂ ಇತರ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಕಾಯವನ್ನು ಅವುಗಳ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿಗಳ ಗುಣಲಬ್ಧಕ್ಕೆ ನೇರ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ಅವುಗಳ ನಡುವಿನ ದೂರದ ವರ್ಗಕ್ಕೆ ವಿಲೋಮ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಆಕರ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: F = Gm₁m₂/r².

say.en: Every body in the universe attracts every other body with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them: F equals Gm 1 metre 2 over r squared. The force acts along the line joining them, and the forces on the two bodies are equal and opposite. For points outside a uniform sphere, the sphere attracts as if all its mass were at its centre. Gravitational force is always attractive.
say.kn: ವಿಶ್ವದ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಕಾಯವೂ ಇತರ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಕಾಯವನ್ನು ಅವುಗಳ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿಗಳ ಗುಣಲಬ್ಧಕ್ಕೆ ನೇರ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ಅವುಗಳ ನಡುವಿನ ದೂರದ ವರ್ಗಕ್ಕೆ ವಿಲೋಮ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಆಕರ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: F equals Gm 1m 2 over r squared.

say.en: Inside a uniform spherical shell the net force is zero.
Forces from several bodies add as vectors superposition.
Two masses attract each other along the line joining them, with equal and opposite forces.
The force is proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance.
Inverse square: double the distance and the force becomes a quarter; triple it and it becomes a ninth.
G is tiny, which is why we never feel the pull between everyday objects. Two 100 kilogram balls a metre apart pull with less than a micronewton.

body.en: G was first measured by Henry Cavendish in 1798 using a torsion balance. Its value is $G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}\,\text{N m}^2\,\text{kg}^{-2}$. It is a universal *constant*, the same everywhere and independent of the medium. Its tiny value is why we never notice the pull between everyday objects.
body.kn: 1798 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆನ್ರಿ ಕ್ಯಾವೆಂಡಿಷ್ ತಿರುಚು ತಕ್ಕಡಿ ಬಳಸಿ G ಯನ್ನು ಮೊದಲ ಬಾರಿಗೆ ಅಳೆದ. G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². ಇದು ಸಾರ್ವತ್ರಿಕ ಸ್ಥಿರಾಂಕ, ಮಾಧ್ಯಮವನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

problem.en: Find the gravitational force between two 50 kg students standing 1 m apart (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).

steps.en: F ≈ 1.67 × 10⁻⁷ N, far too small to notice.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the gravitational force between two 50 kg students standing 1 m apart (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the gravitational force between two 50 kilograms students standing 1 metre apart (G equals 6.67 times 10 to the power minus 11 newtons m squared kg to the power minus 2).
F equals G m 1m 2 divided by r squared equals 6.67 times 10 to the power minus 11 times 50 times 50 divided by 1 squared.
F is approximately 1.67 times 10 to the power minus 7 newtons, far too small to notice.
So the answer is is approximately 1.67 times 10 to the power minus 7 newtons.

problem.en: Two masses attract each other with a force of 36 N. Find the force when the distance between them is tripled.

steps.en: F ∝ 1/r², so tripling r makes F one-ninth.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Two masses attract each other with a force of 36 N. Find the force when the distance between them is tripled.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Two masses attract each other with a force of 36 newtons. Find the force when the distance between them is tripled.
F is proportional to 1 over r squared, so tripling r makes F one-ninth.
F equals 36 over 9 equals 4 newtons.
So the answer is 4 newtons.

body.en: Change r by a factor n and F changes by 1/n². Double both masses and halve the distance: F × 2 × 2 × 4 = 16F.

say.en: Inverse-square scaling. Change r by a factor n and F changes by 1 over n squared. Double both masses and halve the distance: F times 2 times 2 times 4 equals 16F.
